paragraphs: 睜開雙眼，冒險者們感到困惑。除了他們之外，身邊倒了一個人。那人似乎是帶他們來到這裡的嚮導，名叫帕瑞爾・亨德里克斯，但是他死透了。
除此之外，眼前的巨像似乎正在攻擊他們。冒險者們努力與他對抗，卻發現在怎麼用武器攻擊，或是甚至透過魔法，都對他沒什麼影響。那巨像堅不可破，甚至可說是所向無敵。
對戰的同時，冒險者們逐漸想起自己為何會出現在這無助的場景。幾天前，著尼森帝國遭到一群平民推翻，掀起了暴動。皇帝雖然沒死，但已失去了對帝國的控制權。而在反抗的群眾中，由崔尼斯教組成的「崔尼斯的聖騎士」是最大的勢力。

冒險者們受聘於卓尼森帝國的皇帝喬森十三世，奉命找到崔尼斯教的神秘武器，邁爾斯坦巨像，並將其摧毀。傳說中，邁爾斯坦是崔尼斯的弟弟，但在崔尼斯成神後，邁爾斯坦拒絕他的邀約，決定留在凡間，保護崔尼斯的信徒，因此十分受崔尼斯信徒們的愛戴。邁爾斯坦也受到崔尼斯的祝福，以人類之姿活了近兩百歲才死去。在他死後，信徒們建起了一座雕像來紀念他，稱為「邁爾斯坦巨像」。不過隨著時間久遠，邁爾斯坦逐漸被遺忘，巨像的存在也成為了傳說。
隨著與巨像的戰鬥持續著，冒險者們發現自己在所處的平面，似乎是個浮在空中的圓盤，且隨著時間，圓盤邊緣的石塊逐漸剝落，一不小心就會掉下去。而下方，距離大家所熟知的地面極為遙遠。
沃特西掉到了圓盤的邊緣，永恆的墜落下去；拉斐爾被巨像擠壓，斷光了骨頭；哈拉爾德沒能逃過巨像的一拳。最終只剩下苟延殘喘，爬在巨像身上的瑪娜・珍和化身為鳥的歐巴，逃過一劫。在圓盤周圍全數崩塌後，巨像蜷起身體，不動了。瑪娜・珍和歐巴兩人停在巨像頂端，稍作休息。但是他們不知道巨像何時會再動起來，也不知道要怎麼活著回到地面……

瑪娜・珍和歐巴從夢中驚醒，發現自己睡在帳篷中。周圍的沃特西、拉斐爾和哈拉爾德還沒醒來。帳篷被拉開，活生生的帕瑞爾催促著他們，說距離石像只剩一天的路程了，要大家趕快出發。瑪娜・珍和歐巴清楚記得「剛剛」發生的事。叫醒其他夥伴後，大家也對與巨像的戰鬥感到歷歷在目。大家將完全搞不清楚狀況的帕瑞爾打暈了後，歐巴、拉斐爾和哈拉爾德決定要帶著帕瑞爾回到巨像那裡，探索清楚到底發生什麼事；瑪娜・珍和沃特西則決定放棄任務，回去找皇帝索取獎金。
被打到受傷的帕瑞爾走路速度慢了不少，原本一天就會抵達的路程，他們沒能趕上，中間只好停下來過夜。
冒險者們依據記憶中圓盤的範圍估算，在肉眼可見到巨像時，開始擬定戰略。拉斐爾先前往巨像旁，簡單探索是否有什麼魔法或機關，隨後歐巴和哈拉爾德也趕上。接著，拉斐爾透過魔法，要求帕瑞爾攻擊巨像，同時三名冒險者躲到附近的樹林觀察。
圓盤隨著轟隆聲響起而逐漸升起，正如歐巴化為鳥時所見，那並不是個圓盤，而是個圓柱。
一天過去，圓柱已上升到冒險者們看不見他的頂部了。他們計算著這時離開是否安全，然後就聽見「啪」的一聲，一團模糊不清的肉塊從天而降，墜落在圓柱的周圍。那想必是帕瑞爾的屍體了。

沃特西和瑪娜・珍依照記憶，回到了帝國首都桑普塔諾市，但衛兵的穿著似乎變得不太一樣了。詢問了路人後，才知道卓尼森帝國已不復存在，現在是崔尼斯帝國掌權了。瑪娜・珍清楚狀況後，便決定離開這裡，回家去了。沒領到賞金的沃特西很不甘心，透過各種方法，混進了戒備森嚴的王宮內，偽裝成被新聘來上工的平民，並四處尋找金庫的蹤跡。他成功見到了新任的皇帝霍里森一世，告訴他有人要襲擊對他們來說應該很重要的邁爾斯坦巨像。皇帝對於他知道邁爾斯坦巨像這件事感到詫異，但也沒有因此太過慌張，僅派了人去調查而已，沃特西終究沒有得到他想要的獎賞。
拉斐爾、歐巴和哈拉爾德回到了桑普塔諾市，在了解到卓尼森帝國已經瓦解了後，他們很清楚自己的賞金是沒能拿到了（當然，他們也沒能完成任務就是了），於是他們便離開了。
多待了一天，沃特西清楚知道自己在這裡什麼也拿不到，於是他利用機會，將手上的掃把扔了，走出了王宮。首都的居民們各有忙碌的事，沃特西走在路上，沒有什麼人特別關注他，直到他發現自己的肩膀被拍了一下。他回頭，一名披著斗篷，看不見臉的人用手比了個「噓」的手勢。沃特西急忙想問清楚那人是誰？這代表什麼意思？但他只得到了一個模糊的答案：「卓尼森會再回來的。」然後他就昏過去了。
清醒後，他回想起，在昏倒之前，他似乎看見了那斗篷底下一抹微笑，以及聽見一個姓氏：伯納斯。
The adventurers opened their eyes in confusion. A man lay beside them. He appeared to be Parrell Hendrix, the guide who had brought them here, and he was thoroughly dead.
A colossus before them was attacking. The adventurers fought back, but neither weapons nor magic had any effect. The colossus was unbreakable—perhaps invincible.

As they fought, the adventurers gradually remembered why they were trapped in this hopeless scene. Several days earlier, commoners had overthrown the Dranison Empire in a violent uprising. The emperor survived but lost control, and the largest rebel faction was the “Paladins of Trinix,” followers of the Church of Trinix.

Emperor Joson XIII had hired the adventurers to find and destroy the church’s mysterious weapon, the Mylstan Colossus. Legend called Mylstan the younger brother of Trinix. When Trinix became a god, Mylstan declined his invitation and remained in the mortal world to protect Trinix’s faithful, who loved him dearly. Trinix blessed him, allowing him to live nearly two hundred years as a human. After his death, the faithful built a statue in his honor: the Mylstan Colossus. Over time, both Mylstan and the colossus faded into legend.

As the battle continued, the adventurers realized that they stood on a disk floating in the sky. Stones steadily crumbled from its edge, threatening to send anyone nearby plunging toward the familiar ground far below.

WotCy fell from the disk’s edge into an endless descent. The colossus crushed every bone in Raphael’s body. Harald failed to escape its fist. Only Mana Jane, desperately clinging to the statue, and Obba, transformed into a bird, survived. Once the entire disk had collapsed, the colossus curled into itself and stopped moving. Mana Jane and Obba rested atop it, not knowing when it might awaken or how they could return alive to the ground.

Mana Jane and Obba awoke from a dream inside a tent. WotCy, Raphael, and Harald still slept nearby. A living Parrell opened the flap and urged everyone onward, saying the statue was only a day away. Mana Jane and Obba clearly remembered what had “just” happened. Once awakened, their companions also vividly recalled fighting the colossus. They knocked out the utterly confused Parrell. Obba, Raphael, and Harald decided to take him back to the statue and discover the truth, while Mana Jane and WotCy abandoned the mission and returned to demand payment from the emperor.
Injured from the beating, Parrell walked much more slowly. They could not complete the one-day journey and had to camp overnight.

Using their memories to estimate the disk’s radius, the adventurers began planning as soon as the colossus came into view. Raphael approached first to inspect it for magic or mechanisms, followed by Obba and Harald. Raphael then magically compelled Parrell to attack the statue while the three adventurers observed from the nearby woods.
With a thunderous rumble, the disk began rising. As Obba had seen in bird form, it was not a disk at all, but the top of a cylinder.

A day later, the cylinder had risen so high that its top was no longer visible. As the adventurers calculated whether it was safe to leave, a wet smack sounded and an indistinct mass of flesh fell from the sky beside the column. It could only be Parrell’s body.

Following their memories, WotCy and Mana Jane returned to the imperial capital, Samptano, but the guards’ uniforms had changed. A passerby told them that the Dranison Empire no longer existed; the Trinix Empire now ruled. Once she understood, Mana Jane left for home. Bitter at losing his reward, WotCy used every trick he knew to infiltrate the heavily guarded palace, disguised himself as a newly hired common laborer, and searched for the treasury. He reached the new emperor, Horison I, and warned that someone intended to attack the Mylstan Colossus, which should be important to the regime. The emperor was surprised that WotCy knew of it but showed little alarm and merely sent investigators. WotCy never received the reward he wanted.

Raphael, Obba, and Harald also returned to Samptano. Once they learned that the Dranison Empire had collapsed, they knew they would never be paid—though, of course, they had not completed the mission either—so they left.

After one more day, WotCy accepted that there was nothing for him here. He threw away his broom and walked out of the palace. The capital’s people were busy and ignored him until someone tapped his shoulder. WotCy turned to a cloaked, faceless figure holding a finger to its lips. He demanded to know who the stranger was and what this meant, but received only a vague answer: “Dranison will return.” Then he lost consciousness.
When he awoke, he recalled a smile beneath the hood and a surname spoken just before he fainted: Berners.
